locator: I q.11 a.3 co., second proof: Si ergo essent plures dii, oporteret eos differre. Aliquid ergo conveniret uni, quod non alteri
interpretation: Read as a general principle, in its classically equivalent contrapositive: beings that agree in every act are one. 'What belongs' is read as being in act in a respect. This is stronger than the plural-gods case requires (an identity of indiscernibles over acts); a version restricted to totally perfect beings would be equivalent to the conclusion.
